question: Moscovici के 'Social Representations Theory' और Bourdieu के 'Habitus' में स्वास्थ्य विश्वासों को समझाने में क्या मूलभूत अंतर है?

options.text: दोनों identical theoretical frameworks हैं

Social Representations — shared cognitive frameworks (conscious, communicable); Habitus — embodied, pre-reflective dispositions formed by field position — दोनों complementary लेकिन different mechanisms
Bourdieu ने Moscovici को पूरी तरह reject किया
Habitus — individual psychology; Social Representations — only sociology

explanation: Moscovici (1961) — Social Representations: shared mental models जो unfamiliar को familiar बनाते हैं — anchoring + objectification। Communicated through discourse। Bourdieu (1977) — Habitus: field (caste, class position) से historically formed durable dispositions — pre-reflective, embodied ('second nature')। Health belief in: 'TB = curse' — SR level (community discourse); 'cancer is not for us' — habitus (class-based embodied expectation)। Both needed: SR for communication, Habitus for structural reproduction of health inequalities।

question: Stanley Milgram के आज्ञाकारिता (Obedience) प्रयोगों की पद्धतिगत एवं नैतिक आलोचनाओं और उनके 'agentic state' के सिद्धांत का मूल्यांकन करें।

options.text: Milgram के प्रयोग पद्धतिगत और नैतिक दृष्टि से निर्दोष थे
Agentic State — valid construct पर नैतिक violations (deception, distress), ecological validity सीमाएँ, और recent replication debates — complex picture
Milgram के निष्कर्ष — पूरी तरह discredited हो चुके हैं
Agentic state — Bandura के social learning का synonym है

explanation: Milgram (1963-74) — Agentic State: authority system में व्यक्ति autonomous state छोड़कर 'agent' बन जाता है। Criticisms: (1) Ethical — deception, psychological harm (Baumrind critique), (2) Ecological validity — artificial lab, real authority different, (3) Demand characteristics, (4) Gina Perry's archival research — some participants knew shocks were fake। Recent: Burger (2009) partial replication at 45% mark। Counter: situational power of authority remains valid lesson। Health implications: organizational hierarchy and unethical compliance।

question: Critical Health Psychology और mainstream Health Psychology के बीच epistemological tension क्या है?

options.text: कोई tension नहीं — दोनों एक ही approach हैं
Mainstream HP — positivist, individualist, behavior-focused; Critical HP — social constructionist, structural, power-aware, emancipatory — fundamentally different assumptions about health causation
Critical HP — mainstream HP की extension है
Critical HP — anti-scientific है

explanation: Mainstream HP (Matarazzo, Taylor) — positivist, RCT-based, individualist, bio-psychosocial model (still bio-medical adjacent)। Critical HP (Murray, Chamberlain, Marks) — (1) Health = social/political construction, (2) Power differentials और structural inequalities primary, (3) Qualitative, participatory methods, (4) Emancipatory goals — not just behavior change but social transformation। Tension: Can you simultaneously study individual behavior AND structural oppression? Feminist HP, Community HP, Liberation HP — all within critical tradition। India में: tribal health आंदोलन = critical HP।

question: Giddens का 'Structuration Theory' सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में 'agency vs structure' बहस को कैसे हल करने का प्रयास करता है?

options.text: Giddens — structure को agency पर absolute priority देते हैं
Structure और Agency — duality, not dualism: agents structure को reproduce करते हैं और structure agency को enable/constrain करती है — recursive relationship
Giddens — methodological individualism के समर्थक हैं
Structuration Theory — health behavior research में inapplicable है

explanation: Anthony Giddens (1984) — Structuration Theory: Structure (rules + resources) → dual: enables AND constrains। Agency → reproduces structure (but can transform)। Recursive duality — not determinism, not voluntarism। Health Application: ASHA worker (agent) operates within PHC structure (constraints) but can innovate (agency) → over time, successful innovations become new structural rules। Health behavior: individual choices within structural constraints (Bourdieu field similar but more power-focused)। Practical consciousness vs discursive consciousness।

question: Weick का 'Sensemaking' सिद्धांत और Luhmann का 'Systems Theory' स्वास्थ्य संगठनों में संचार संकट को कैसे समझाते हैं?

options.text: दोनों theories health organizations में irrelevant हैं

Sensemaking — equivocal situations में meaning construction (retrospective, enactive); Systems Theory — autopoietic organizations self-referentially communicate — both explain why health crises are mismanaged
Sensemaking और Systems Theory — identical explanations देते हैं
Luhmann की Systems Theory — psychological reductionism है

explanation: Weick (1995) — Sensemaking: enactment (situations are partly created by actors), selection (narrative making), retention। Health crisis: COVID response — officials making sense of ambiguous data, retroactive justification। 7 properties: Social, Retrospective, Enactive, Cues-based, etc। Luhmann — Autopoietic Systems: organizations self-reproduce through communication। Health system as autopoietic — resists environmental perturbation (external advice). Coupling: health system poorly coupled to community concerns। Together: explain why top-down health directives fail in crisis।

question: Norman Fairclough की 'Critical Discourse Analysis' (CDA) का उपयोग स्वास्थ्य नीति में power और ideology को कैसे reveal करता है?

options.text: CDA — केवल linguistic analysis है, power से असंबंधित
CDA दिखाता है कि health policy documents में language ideological choices को normalize करती है — 'individual responsibility' discourse structural factors को obscure करता है
CDA — health policy में objective analysis है
Fairclough के CDA को health research में apply नहीं किया जा सकता

explanation: Fairclough (1992) — CDA: text + discursive practice + social practice। Three-dimensional analysis। Health policy in: (1) 'Lifestyle diseases' framing → individual blame, structural factors invisible, (2) 'Health-seeking behavior' → pathologizes poor communities rather than poor services, (3) 'Target groups' → dehumanization, (4) 'Compliance' → paternalism. India में: National Health Policy documents — 'wellness' discourse और 'personal responsibility' language → poverty/caste as health determinants कम visible। CDA unmasks these power effects।

question: 'Intersubjectivity' (Husserl, Merleau-Ponty) की अवधारणा सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में health interactions को कैसे enrich करती है?

options.text: Intersubjectivity — philosophical concept, empirical health research में irrelevant
Shared meaning-making और embodied understanding — health encounters में provider-patient 'meeting of worlds' → therapeutic alliance की philosophical foundation
Intersubjectivity — केवल linguistic communication है
Phenomenology और social psychology — unrelated disciplines

explanation: Husserl — Intersubjectivity: shared phenomenal world। Merleau-Ponty — embodied intersubjectivity: pre-reflective, bodily resonance। Health Application: (1) Therapeutic relationship requires genuine 'meeting' — not just information transfer, (2) Nurses' embodied attunement to patient's distress, (3) Empathy as intersubjective phenomenon (not just cognitive perspective-taking), (4) Pain communication — words inadequate, intersubjective understanding needed। IPA (Interpretive Phenomenological Analysis) in health psychology draws on this। Beyond positivist patient-as-object।

question: Albert Bandura के 'Self-Efficacy Theory' की सीमाओं का आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन करें और बताएं कि यह structural health inequalities को क्यों adequately explain नहीं कर पाती।

options.text: Self-Efficacy Theory — कोई सीमा नहीं है
SE — individualist, decontextualizes agency from structural constraints, conflates confidence with real opportunity, और may victim-blame — structural interventions equally necessary
SE Theory — health behavior research में completely discredited
SE का structural factors से कोई interaction नहीं

explanation: Self-Efficacy criticisms: (1) Individualism — ignores structural barriers (poverty cannot be 'believed away'), (2) Paradox: high SE in resource-poor environments → frustration when blocked by structures, (3) Cultural variation — collectivist cultures में individual SE less relevant than collective, (4) Measurement issues — domain-specific vs generalized, (5) SE alone does not predict action when resources absent। Feminist critique: women's low SE = rational response to real powerlessness, not cognitive deficit। Solutions: Structural + Collective Efficacy interventions alongside individual SE building।

question: George Herbert Mead का 'Symbolic Interactionism' और Charles Peirce का 'Semiotics' — दोनों मिलकर स्वास्थ्य संचार को कैसे inform करते हैं?

options.text: Symbolic Interactionism और Semiotics — health में inapplicable philosophical theories
Meaning creation through symbols/signs in social interaction — health messages' symbolic content और shared meaning-making process को reveal करते हैं
दोनों theories एक ही हैं
Semiotics — केवल advertising में applicable है

explanation: Mead (1934) — Symbolic Interactionism: 'I' and 'Me', significant symbols, role-taking। Meaning arises from social interaction। Peirce — Sign = Representamen + Object + Interpretant। Health Communication: (1) Red cross symbol — icon (resembles) + index + symbol। (2) Health campaign images — symbolic meaning varies by community (needle = fear vs. healing), (3) Doctor's white coat — symbol of authority/trust (contested), (4) 'Healthy body' images in IEC — whose symbolic standard? SI + Semiotics → messages must be socially constructed WITH target community — not AT them।

question: Jonathan Turner की 'Theory of Motivation, Emotion, and Emotional Energy' का स्वास्थ्य संगठनों में worker motivation पर क्या निहितार्थ है?

options.text: Turner की theory — केवल macro-sociological है, organizations में irrelevant
Emotional energy (Collins) + Interaction Ritual Chains — successful health encounters build shared EE; failed encounters deplete workers and communities
Turner की theory Freud के motivation theory का extension है
Emotional Energy — physical energy का synonym है

explanation: Randall Collins (2004) — Interaction Ritual Chains: face-to-face encounters with shared focus + emotional entrainment → emotional energy (EE). High EE → enthusiasm, solidarity, confidence। Health Application: Positive community health meetings → shared EE → ASHA workers more motivated। Failed encounters (disrespect, exclusion) → EE drain → demoralization। Implications: (1) Regular community health rituals (VHSNDs), (2) Peer support meetings, (3) Recognition ceremonies, (4) 'Ritual solidarity' in health teams。 Turner adds: need satisfaction (identity, belonging, security) drives participation।

question: 'Narrative Medicine' (Rita Charon) और सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में 'narrative identity' (McAdams) का health में क्या योगदान है?

options.text: Narratives — health में anecdotal, evidence-free approach
Illness narratives capture subjective experience, restore agency, facilitate meaning-making और improve provider empathy — complementing biomedical evidence
Narrative Medicine — केवल literary exercise है
Narrative identity — केवल childhood में relevant है

explanation: Rita Charon (2001) — Narrative Medicine: close reading of patient stories → enhanced clinical empathy, recognition of suffering, ethical action। McAdams (1993) — Personal narrative as identity: life = internalized, evolving story। Illness disrupts narrative → 'biographical disruption' (Bury). Narrative reconstruction = central to chronic illness adjustment। Health Applications: (1) Life story interviews in geriatric care, (2) Cancer patients' meaning-making through writing, (3) Medical education — narrative competence, (4) Community health — testimonials as social proof। Kleinman's 'illness narrative' also foundational।

question: Pierre Bourdieu के 'Field Theory' में 'Capital' (Economic, Cultural, Social, Symbolic) का स्वास्थ्य असमानताओं को पुनरुत्पादित करने में क्या भूमिका है?

options.text: Bourdieu का Capital — केवल economic resources
Multiple capitals interact: cultural (health literacy), social (networks), symbolic (respectability) — lower capitals → health field में marginalization → inequalities reproduced across generations
Bourdieu की theory — individualist है
Health field में केवल economic capital relevant है

explanation: Bourdieu — Field Theory in health: Health field = structured space of positions। Capital forms: (1) Economic — money for healthcare, (2) Cultural — embodied (health literacy, body practices), institutionalized (degrees), objectified (books), (3) Social — networks to doctors, (4) Symbolic — 'good patient' respectability। Low capitals → misrecognition of health system norms, symbolic violence ('why didn't you come earlier?')। Habitus-capital-field intersection → explains why health inequalities are reproduced। Dalit + low economic + low cultural capital → triple disadvantage।

question: 'Intersectionality' के Crenshaw (legal) और Hill Collins (matrix of domination) के formulations में सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान की health research में क्या methodological implications हैं?

options.text: Intersectionality — only qualitative research में applicable
दोनों demand multiplicative (not additive) analysis — health data को multiple simultaneous axes (caste+gender+class+disability) पर simultaneously examine करना
Crenshaw और Collins की frameworks identical हैं
Intersectionality — quantitative health research में impossible है

explanation: Crenshaw (1989) — legal contexts: intersection makes Black women invisible (not Black enough for some claims, not woman enough for others)। Collins (1990) — Matrix of Domination: interlocking systems of oppression (race, class, gender, sexuality) operating simultaneously at structural, disciplinary, hegemonic, interpersonal levels। Methodological implications: (1) Disaggregate data by multiple axes, (2) Interaction terms in quantitative analysis, (3) Avoid single-identity analysis, (4) Community-participatory methods। India: SC+female+rural+disabled — intersectional disadvantage in health outcomes।

question: 'Epidemiology of Syndemics' (Singer) और सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में 'structural violence' (Farmer) — दोनों मिलकर health disparities को कैसे explain करते हैं?

options.text: Syndemics — केवल concurrent diseases का concept है
Syndemics: diseases interact biologically AND through shared social conditions; Structural Violence: political-economic structures cause suffering → together expose health inequality's root causes
Structural Violence — केवल war-related concept
दोनों frameworks competing, complementary नहीं

explanation: Merrill Singer (1994) — Syndemic Theory: substance abuse + violence + AIDS (SAVA syndemic) — disease clusters interact in social context (poverty, inequality)। Not merely comorbidity — biologically synergistic AND socially determined। Paul Farmer (2003) — Structural Violence: political-economic structures systematically harm poor, marginalized (TB/HIV in Haiti)। Together: poverty → substance abuse + violence → HIV + TB syndemic (India में: malnutrition + TB + poverty + gender inequality = syndemic). Both demand social transformation, not just biomedical treatment।

question: Solomon Asch के conformity experiments की कौन-सी methodological limitations हैं और इनके cross-cultural replications ने क्या reveal किया?

options.text: Asch experiments — कोई limitation नहीं, perfectly replicated worldwide
Lab artificiality, US WEIRD sample, sex composition, perceived stakes — cross-cultural: collectivist cultures में higher conformity, but effect universal — situational power confirmed
Cross-cultural replications ने Asch के निष्कर्षों को completely refuted किया
Conformity — केवल American societies में होती है

explanation: Asch (1951-56) — Limitations: (1) Artificial task (obvious correct answer) → ecological validity low, (2) All-male US participants — WEIRD bias, (3) Low stakes — real decisions different, (4) Demand characteristics, (5) Only public conformity measured, not private acceptance। Cross-cultural: Bond & Smith (1996) meta-analysis — collectivist cultures (Japan, China) → higher conformity; individualistic → lower। But conformity exists everywhere — situationally determined. Face-saving cultures: conformity more about harmony than ignorance। Health in: treatment decision conformity to family norms (India)।

question: 'Symbolic Threat Theory' और 'Integrated Threat Theory' (Stephan) का उपयोग करके India में COVID-19 के दौरान community-level stigma और xenophobia को explain करें।

options.text: COVID stigma — purely individual psychological phenomenon है
Realistic threats (disease) + Symbolic threats (cultural pollution beliefs) + Negative stereotypes + Intergroup anxiety → scapegoating of specific communities — documented in India 2020
Threat theories — COVID context में inapplicable
COVID stigma केवल ignorance के कारण था

explanation: COVID India 2020: (1) Realistic threat — viral spread fear, (2) Symbolic threat — certain communities 'polluting' India's spiritual/cultural body, (3) Negative stereotypes — 'superspreader' communities, (4) Intergroup anxiety — proximity fears। Tablighi Jamaat → scapegoating. Northeast people → anti-Asian discrimination. Health workers attacked. Stephan's ITT: all 4 threat types activated → violence, discrimination, treatment refusal. Solutions: accurate threat information, intergroup contact, leader condemnation of scapegoating, humanizing communications।

question: Foucault के 'Medical Gaze' (Le Regard Médical) की अवधारणा का आधुनिक digital health surveillance और patient data में क्या अनुप्रयोग है?

options.text: Medical Gaze — 19th century concept, आज irrelevant
Medical Gaze (objectifying, disciplining patient bodies) digital health में intensified: AI diagnostics, fitness trackers, health apps → panopticon of health data, surveillance capitalism
Digital health — medical gaze को eliminate करता है
Foucault — health में only historical analysis दिया

explanation: Foucault (1963) — 'Birth of the Clinic': Medical Gaze transforms patient from person to body-as-object. Clinic as disciplinary space. Digital extension: (1) Fitness trackers → continuous self-surveillance (internalized gaze), (2) AI diagnostics → patient as data point, (3) Health apps collecting intimate data → corporate surveillance capitalism (Zuboff), (4) Aarogya Setu/ABHA → state health surveillance, (5) Predictive profiling — insurance discrimination। Biopolitics (Foucault) → algorithmic governance of populations। Privacy, consent, data justice concerns।

question: James Pennebaker का 'Expressive Writing' research क्या reveal करता है और इसके neurobiological mechanisms क्या हैं?

options.text: Expressive Writing — unproven, purely anecdotal
Writing about trauma → cognitive processing, narrative coherence, emotional regulation → improved immune function, health outcomes — inhibition model और self-regulatory model से explained
Expressive Writing — केवल mental health में, physical health में नहीं
Expressive Writing — केवल educated, literate populations के लिए

explanation: Pennebaker & Beall (1986) — Paradigm: write about deepest thoughts/feelings about trauma for 15 mins, 4 days → improved immune function, fewer health centre visits, better mood. Meta-analyses support moderate effects। Mechanisms: (1) Inhibition model — actively inhibiting thoughts → physiological burden; writing releases, (2) Cognitive processing — narrative coherence reduces intrusive thoughts, (3) Emotional regulation (Gross), (4) Neurobiologically: reduced HPA activation, improved NK cell function। Limitations: cultural (collectivism), literacy, moderators। India में: adapted oral storytelling versions।

question: सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में 'Social Comparison Theory' के extensions — 'Temporal Self-Appraisal' (Wilson & Ross) और 'Social Projection' (Krueger) — chronic illness management में क्या भूमिका निभाते हैं?

options.text: दोनों concepts chronic illness में irrelevant हैं

Temporal Self-Appraisal (past self vs current) और Social Projection (assuming others similar) — chronic illness में identity continuity, optimistic projection और self-serving comparisons को explain करते हैं
Social Projection — always maladaptive in illness
TSA और Social Projection — identical concepts हैं

explanation: Wilson & Ross (2001) — Temporal Self-Appraisal: past self unfavorably appraised to feel better about present ('मैं तब भी इतना बीमार था, अब बेहतर हूँ')। Adaptive in chronic illness — self-continuity maintained. Krueger — Social Projection: assuming others share one's characteristics. In illness: projecting pain experience onto others → validation-seeking, social comparison for normalization। Chronic illness: downward temporal comparisons (better than 3 months ago) + peer comparisons (SHGs) → coping। But: unrealistic optimism through projection → treatment non-adherence।

question: 'Terror Management Health Model' (Goldenberg & Arndt) mortality salience का health behaviors पर कैसे paradoxical प्रभाव दिखाती है?

options.text: Mortality salience हमेशा health-protective behaviors बढ़ाती है
Mortality Salience → defensive responding — tanning, smoking, ignoring health threats — to affirm cultural worldview या escape body-awareness; health messages backfire
TMHM — TMT का direct extension है, नई insights नहीं देती
Mortality Salience — health behaviors से सीधे-सीधे जुड़ी नहीं है

explanation: Goldenberg & Arndt (2008) — TMHM: mortality salience activates two conflicting responses: (1) Death reminder → health behaviors (protective), BUT (2) Health messages often remind of bodily mortality → defensive: (a) worldview defense (cultural practices overriding health), (b) body transcendence (ignoring physical body), (c) risk behaviors affirming symbolic immortality। Skin cancer awareness + MS → MORE tanning (worldview: tanned = attractive, alive). Cigarettes in warrior cultures = symbolic. Implications: health messages should avoid mortality salience OR provide clear cultural worldview bolstering।

question: Jonathan Haidt का 'Social Intuitionist Model' (SIM) नैतिक निर्णयों को कैसे explain करता है और यह स्वास्थ्य नैतिकता में क्यों महत्वपूर्ण है?

options.text: SIM — नैतिक reasoning primary, intuition secondary मानता है
Moral intuitions come first (fast, automatic) → post-hoc reasoning; reasoning rarely changes moral judgments — health ethics decisions इसी से driven हैं
SIM — Kohlberg के moral development theory का extension
SIM — केवल clinical ethics में, public health में नहीं

explanation: Haidt (2001) — SIM: 'Moral intuitions come first and moral reasoning comes later.' The reasoning is mostly post-hoc rationalization of intuitive reactions। Dumbfounding phenomenon। Moral foundations: care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity, liberty। Health ethics implications: (1) Disgust (sanctity foundation) → irrational rejection of organ donation, (2) Authority → vaccine hesitancy if 'authority' changes advice, (3) In-group loyalty → prioritize own community in triage, (4) Care → universal healthcare intuition। Ethics committees must acknowledge intuitive reasoning underlying 'rational' debates।

question: Walter Mischel के 'Personality Coherence Paradox' और 'CAPS Model' स्वास्थ्य व्यवहार की consistency और context-specificity को कैसे explain करते हैं?

options.text: Personality traits — सदैव health behavior को predict करते हैं
CAPS: person × situation interactions — health behaviors are if-then situation-specific patterns, not cross-situationally consistent traits — personalized interventions needed
CAPS Model — Big Five को replace करती है
Mischel ने personality को completely dismiss किया

explanation: Mischel (1968) — Personality Paradox: cross-situational consistency of behavior much lower than assumed (r ≈ 0.3). CAPS (1995) — Cognitive-Affective Processing System: internal units (encodings, expectancies, affects, goals, competencies) → if-then behavioral signatures (IF this situation THEN this behavior)। Health: 'I exercise' NOT consistent — IF with friends, THEN exercise; IF alone/stressed, THEN skip। Personalized health interventions: identify if-then patterns, engineer situations. 'Implementation intentions' (Gollwitzer) = CAPS-informed。

question: सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में 'Network Contagion Theory' (Christakis & Fowler) का स्वास्थ्य व्यवहार के प्रसार में क्या योगदान और क्या controversies हैं?

options.text: Network Contagion — केवल infectious disease में applicable
Health behaviors (obesity, smoking, happiness) spread through social networks up to 3 degrees of separation — criticized for confounding (homophily, shared environment) but influential
Christakis & Fowler के findings — fully replicated without controversy
Social networks — health behavior में irrelevant हैं

explanation: Christakis & Fowler (2007-2008): Obesity, smoking cessation, happiness spread through social networks — up to 3 degrees (friend of friend of friend)। Claimed mechanisms: norm influence, behavioral mimicry। Controversies: (1) Homophily confound — similar people cluster, (2) Shared environmental causes, (3) Statistical methodology (Cohen-Cole & Fletcher critique), (4) Causal inference impossible from observational data। Despite criticism: idea influential — Network interventions — target hubs and bridges। Social contagion in health SBCC programs। Ego-alter network approaches in India's health promotion।

question: 'Self-Determination Theory' (Deci & Ryan) में 'Autonomy Support' बनाम 'Control' health communication strategies में क्यों निर्णायक है और इसका cross-cultural validity क्या है?

options.text: SDT — केवल Western individualistic cultures में valid है
Autonomy-supportive contexts → identified/integrated regulation → more durable behavior change; controlling → introjection/external → fragile; SDT universal though expression culturally varies
SDT में autonomy और control — interchangeable concepts हैं
SDT — mental health में, physical health behavior में irrelevant

explanation: Deci & Ryan (1985, 2000) — SDT: Needs: Autonomy + Competence + Relatedness. Regulatory continuum: External → Introjected → Identified → Integrated (autonomous motivation). Autonomy Support: rationale provision, perspective-taking, non-controlling language → internalization। Controlling communication → reactance, pressure experience, rebound. Cross-cultural: needs universal; autonomy expression varies — in collectivist cultures, autonomy = acting in harmony with family values (not Western individualism). Health in: MI is autonomy-supportive। India में: family-based autonomy support for treatment adherence。

question: Elias Canetti का 'Crowds and Power' और Le Bon की 'Crowd Psychology' की तुलना करें और बताएं कि स्वास्थ्य आपदाओं में crowd behavior को कैसे समझाया जाता है।

options.text: Le Bon और Canetti — identical theories हैं
Le Bon — crowd as irrational, primitive; Canetti — crowds as liberating, power-seeking; modern: emergent norm theory (Turner) is more nuanced — crowds are NOT mindless
Crowd Psychology — health emergencies में irrelevant है
Crowds — always destructive in health contexts

explanation: Le Bon (1895) — crowds: contagion, suggestibility, regression to primitive। Criticized: racial bias, authoritarian implications, empirically wrong। Canetti (1960) — crowds: 4 types (open/closed/slow/quick); density → equality, liberation from individual isolation। Modern: Turner & Killian (1957) — Emergent Norm Theory: crowds develop shared norms contextually — NOT mindless. Reicher (1987) — Social Identity Model of Crowd Behavior। Health: Kumbh Mela COVID risk; vaccine distribution stampedes; Rath Yatra COVID. Crowd management: information + legitimate authority + trust + space design।

question: Nancy Fraser का 'Participatory Parity' सिद्धांत और Axel Honneth का 'Recognition Theory' सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान और health equity में कैसे योगदान करते हैं?

options.text: दोनों theories — political philosophy में, health में irrelevant

Recognition Theory: misrecognition (contempt, invisibility) → psychological harm + social exclusion → health disparities; Participatory Parity: equal participation in healthcare decisions as justice requirement
Fraser और Honneth की theories — identical हैं
Recognition — केवल cultural dimension है, health से unrelated

explanation: Honneth (1992) — Recognition Theory: 3 domains: Love (care, self-confidence), Legal recognition (rights, self-respect), Social esteem (solidarity, self-esteem)। Misrecognition: maltreatment, rights violations, denigration → moral injuries → health outcomes। Fraser (2000) — Participatory Parity: redistribution (economic) + recognition (cultural) + representation (political) together needed. Health application: Dalit patients misrecognized in hospitals (contempt) → late presentation, non-adherence। ASHA workers misrecognized as 'volunteers' not 'workers' → exploitation. Recognition + representation + redistribution = health justice।

question: 'Polyvagal Theory' (Porges) का सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान और community health interventions के design में क्या महत्व है?

options.text: Polyvagal Theory — केवल individual therapy में applicable
Neuroception (threat/safety cues) → autonomic state → social engagement capacity — safe social environments enable prosocial behavior और healing — community design में critical
Polyvagal Theory — psychoanalytic theory है
Autonomic nervous system — social behavior से unrelated है

explanation: Stephen Porges (1994) — Polyvagal Theory: 3 neural circuits: (1) Ventral vagal (safe, social engagement — co-regulation, prosocial), (2) Sympathetic (fight-flight), (3) Dorsal vagal (freeze, shutdown)। Neuroception — unconscious assessment of safety/danger। Social Applications: (1) Trauma-informed environments must signal safety (calm staff, warm welcome, predictable routines), (2) Unsafe PHC environments → sympathetic/dorsal states → poor communication, non-compliance, (3) VHSND design — safety cues enable genuine participation, (4) Co-regulation — calm health worker regulates patient state. Community as 'container of safety'।

question: Amartya Sen के 'Capability Approach' और Martha Nussbaum के 'Central Capabilities' का सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में कैसा संगम है?

options.text: Capability Approach — केवल economics में, psychology में नहीं
Capabilities = real freedoms to be/do — health psychology में agency, flourishing और well-being को GDP/utility से परे operationalize करता है; misrecognition = capability deprivation
Sen और Nussbaum — competing, incompatible frameworks
Capability Approach — मनोवैज्ञानिक well-being से unrelated है

explanation: Sen (1985, 1999) — Capabilities: functionings (achieved states) + capabilities (real freedoms to achieve)। Nussbaum (2000) — 10 Central Capabilities including bodily health, emotional development, social affiliation. Psychology link: (1) Self-efficacy ≠ real capability (structural constraints), (2) Psychological well-being requires capability threshold, (3) Agency = key psychological function + capability, (4) Adaptive preferences (oppressed prefer what they can get) — preference satisfaction theories miss hidden deprivation। India में: NFHS capabilities analysis — women's health capabilities severely constrained by gender norms।

question: Vygotsky के 'Zone of Proximal Development' और 'Scaffolding' को community health education में कैसे apply किया जाता है और इसकी limitations क्या हैं?

options.text: ZPD — केवल children's cognitive development के लिए
ZPD applied to adult community health: ASHA scaffolding community members' health behaviors beyond their current capacity — cultural tools mediate; criticized for ignoring power dynamics
Scaffolding — Bandura के modeling के identical है
Vygotsky की sociocultural theory — health में inapplicable है

explanation: Vygotsky (1934) — ZPD: what learner can do with guidance - what alone. Scaffolding (Wood, Bruner): temporary support → internalization → removal। Cultural tools (language, concepts) mediate learning। Adult health education: (1) ASHA guides community through immunization schedule (scaffold) → community internalizes, (2) Peer support groups — advanced members scaffold newcomers, (3) PLA facilitators scaffold community health analysis। Criticisms: (1) Ignores power asymmetry in scaffold relationship, (2) Cultural tools are not neutral (whose knowledge?), (3) Freire's critique — scaffolding can still be 'banking model'।

question: George Kelly का 'Personal Construct Theory' और health psychology में 'Repertory Grid Technique' का diagnostic एवं therapeutic value क्या है?

options.text: PCT — केवल personality research में, clinical health में नहीं
PCT: people as scientists constructing experience — health constructs (threat/safety, control/helplessness) guide illness behavior; RepGrid reveals idiosyncratic meaning systems
Repertory Grid — only quantitative data देती है, qualitative insights नहीं
Personal Construct Theory — CBT का subset है

explanation: George Kelly (1955) — PCT: Each person = scientist with unique construct system. Health constructs: 'strength vs weakness', 'normal vs sick', 'controllable vs chance'. Tight vs loose constructions. Repertory Grid: elements (significant people/situations) × constructs (bipolar dimensions) → individual's meaning matrix. Health Applications: (1) Cancer patients' illness constructs predict coping, (2) Chronic pain — constructs about pain (challenge vs punishment), (3) Fixed Role Therapy for health behavior change, (4) Doctor-patient construct clash. India में: 'fate vs karma' construction of illness → fatalistic health behavior।

question: Erving Goffman के 'Stigma Management Strategies' में से कौन-सी strategies chronic illness वाले individuals के psychological well-being पर negative impact डालती हैं?

options.text: सभी Goffman की stigma management strategies — positive outcomes देती हैं
Passing (hiding stigma), Covering (reducing salience) और Withdrawal — short-term shame relief पर long-term isolation, identity distress, और help-seeking avoidance उत्पन्न करती हैं
Disclosure — always harmful strategy है
Stigma management — HIV में inapplicable है

explanation: Goffman (1963) — Stigma Management: Discredited (visible) vs Discreditable (concealable). Strategies: (1) Passing — concealing stigma identity (HIV, mental illness, epilepsy) → constant vigilance, cognitive load, isolation, (2) Covering — disclosed but minimizing (wheelchair → 'only sometimes'), (3) Withdrawal — avoid contact with 'normals' → social isolation। Alternative: Identity disclosure + advocacy (activism) → better psychological outcomes (Corrigan — Coming Out model). India में: TB/HIV patients' passing → delayed treatment, partner notification failure। Selective disclosure + social support → better outcomes।

question: Reintegrative Shaming Theory (Braithwaite) का स्वास्थ्य नीति में क्या निहितार्थ है?

options.text: Shaming — health behavior change में always effective
Stigmatizing shaming → defiance/isolation; Reintegrative shaming (communitarian, followed by forgiveness/re-inclusion) → behavior change — health context में distinction critical
Braithwaite's theory — criminal justice में only
Shame — always dysfunctional in health contexts

explanation: Braithwaite (1989) — Reintegrative Shaming: Stigmatizing (labeling, outcasting) → recidivism/defiance। Reintegrative (shaming the behavior, not person, followed by acceptance back into community) → behavior change in communitarian societies। Health applications: (1) ODF campaign — stigmatizing open defecators → ostracization = stigmatizing shaming → backfire, (2) TB isolation without reintegration — stigmatizing, (3) Alcohol rehabilitation with community ceremony of reintegration — potentially reintegrative, (4) Obesity shaming → worse health behaviors. Requires strong community bonds (communitarianism) to work।

question: Habermas का 'Communicative Action Theory' और 'Lifeworld vs System' सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में health service delivery को कैसे critique करता है?

options.text: Habermas — health में inapplicable है
Health system (money + administrative power) colonizing lifeworld (lived health experience) → technocratic, dehumanizing care; communicative rationality needed to restore meaningful health encounters
Lifeworld और System — health में complementary without tension
Habermas — Weber के bureaucracy theory का synonym है

explanation: Habermas (1984) — Theory of Communicative Action: Lifeworld (symbolic reproduction — culture, society, personality) vs System (material reproduction — money, power, bureaucracy). Colonization: system rationality invades lifeworld → distortion of communicative action। Health Application: (1) Biomedical technocracy → patient as organ/target, (2) Insurance/administrative systems → physician's time for real listening eroded, (3) PHC metrics (deliveries, immunizations) → ASHA performs tasks without community relationship, (4) PPI (Patient and Public Involvement) attempts to restore communicative rationality।

question: Triandis का 'Subjective Culture' और 'Social Behavior' model — cross-cultural health psychology में क्या methodological contributions देता है?

options.text: Triandis का model — Hofstede के Cultural Dimensions के identical है
Subjective Culture (shared cognitive + affective elements) distinguishes attitudes, roles, norms, values और isomorphism between cultures — richer than dimensional models for health research
Triandis — केवल individualism-collectivism का विस्तार करते हैं
Subjective Culture — objective culture का subset है

explanation: Harry Triandis (1972) — Subjective Culture: group's characteristic way of perceiving social environment — shared attitudes, beliefs, roles, norms, values. Not just dimensions but rich fabric. Allocentrism vs idiocentrism (within-culture variations). Method: functional equivalence — same construct may need different measures across cultures. Health: illness cognitions differ in subjective culture (not just country). Cross-cultural health interventions must assess local subjective culture — not assume Hofstede dimensions sufficient. India में: state-level subjective culture variations in health seeking patterns।

question: John Cacioppo का 'Loneliness Research' और 'Social Neuroscience' ने सामाजिक अलगाव के health consequences को कैसे mechanistically explain किया?

options.text: Loneliness — केवल subjective feeling है, biological mechanisms नहीं
Loneliness → hypervigilance to social threat + HPA activation + inflammatory dysregulation + sleep disruption + accelerated cognitive decline — evolutionary threat-detection account
Cacioppo का loneliness research — replication में failed
Social isolation — mental health में, physical health में नहीं

explanation: Cacioppo & Patrick (2008) — Loneliness as evolutionary threat signal: isolated individual = vulnerable → threat hypervigilance. Mechanisms: (1) Heightened neural threat sensitivity (amygdala), (2) HPA axis dysregulation → chronic cortisol → immunosuppression, (3) Pro-inflammatory gene expression, (4) Sleep fragmentation, (5) Accelerated cognitive decline, (6) Cardiovascular risk. Social neuroscience: lonely brain encodes world differently (threat-bias). Population-level: loneliness epidemic in elderly India — widows, migrants, nuclear families. Social prescribing — community connections as medicine।

question: Fiske का 'Core Social Motives' model health behavior में कैसे apply होता है?

options.text: Fiske के social motives — health में irrelevant हैं
Belonging, Understanding, Controlling, Enhancing Self, Trusting — पाँच motives health encounters को drive करते हैं और इन्हें threaten करने से poor outcomes होते हैं
Fiske — केवल 3 social motives describe करते हैं
Core Social Motives — Maslow की hierarchy का extension है

explanation: Susan Fiske (2004) — 5 Core Social Motives: (1) Belonging — need for social inclusion, (2) Understanding — need for shared meaning, (3) Controlling — sense of personal efficacy, (4) Enhancing Self — positive self-image, (5) Trusting — default positive view of others. Health: (1) Illness threatens belonging → social support groups address, (2) Diagnosis threatens understanding → clear explanation needed, (3) Chronic illness threatens control → shared decision-making restores, (4) Stigma threatens self-enhancement → positive identity work, (5) Medical system distrust → trust-building interventions। All 5 must be addressed for therapeutic alliance।

question: 'Epigenetic Social Psychology' में social experiences कैसे gene expression को alter करती हैं और इसके health equity के लिए क्या implications हैं?

options.text: Epigenetics — pure biology है, social psychology से unrelated

Social stress (discrimination, poverty, early adversity) → DNA methylation + histone modification → altered gene expression → health outcomes — AND transmissible across generations (transgenerational epigenetics)
Epigenetic changes — irreversible हैं
Social epigenetics — hypothesis only, no evidence yet

explanation: Social Epigenetics (Hertzman, 2000; McEwen, 2012): Social exposures → epigenetic marks → altered biological functioning. Examples: (1) Early adversity → CpG methylation in glucocorticoid receptor gene → HPA dysregulation for life, (2) Racial discrimination → accelerated epigenetic aging (Telomere shortening), (3) Poverty → inflammatory gene expression patterns, (4) Transgenerational: Holocaust survivors' children show epigenetic stress signatures. India में: Dalit communities → discrimination → epigenetic load → health disparities that persist even with income increase. Justice interventions must begin prenatally।

question: Karl Weick का 'High Reliability Organizations' (HRO) सिद्धांत और Reason का 'Swiss Cheese Model' स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली की सुरक्षा में कैसे apply होते हैं?

options.text: दोनों models — aviation में only, health में nahi
HRO: preoccupation with failure, sensitivity to operations, reluctance to simplify, commitment to resilience — SCM: multiple defensive layers prevent latent errors from causing harm
Swiss Cheese Model — human error को ignore करता है
HROs — errors नहीं होते

explanation: Weick et al. — HRO: 5 mindful organizing principles for high-stakes systems। (1) Preoccupation with failure (report near-misses), (2) Reluctance to simplify (complex problems need complex understanding), (3) Sensitivity to operations (frontline awareness), (4) Commitment to resilience (recover from errors), (5) Deference to expertise (not hierarchy)। James Reason (1990) — Swiss Cheese: active failures (human error) + latent failures (organizational). Holes align → accident. Health: medication errors, surgical mishaps, lab failures. India में: patient safety WHO protocols; adverse event reporting systems। Human factors approach।

question: 'Anthropology of Suffering' (Kleinman, Das, Lock) और सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान का मिलकर chronic suffering communities को health interventions कैसे design करते हैं?

options.text: Suffering — only medical/clinical domain है
Social suffering (political-economic forces cause embodied distress); illness narratives; cultural idioms of distress — interventions must witness, not just treat suffering
Anthropology of Suffering और Social Psychology — competing frameworks हैं
Chronic suffering communities — only pharmacological interventions need करते हैं

explanation: Kleinman et al. (1997) — Social Suffering: misery caused by political violence, poverty, displacement → embodied. Veena Das — Critical Events: extreme violence redefines ordinary life. Margaret Lock — Local biologies: suffering embodied differently across cultures. Social psych contributions: (1) Narrative witness — hearing suffering → acknowledgment, (2) Community ritual for collective processing (Van der Kolk), (3) Social support mobilization, (4) Political advocacy as therapeutic action (Becker, Fanon). India में: post-communal violence mental health → community healing rituals + trauma-informed care। 'Presence' not just 'intervention'।

question: 'Discursive Psychology' (Harré, Potter & Wetherell) mainstream social cognition research को कैसे challenge करती है?

options.text: Discursive Psychology — social cognition का extension है
Discursive Psychology: attitudes, identities, mental states are NOT internal representations but discursive constructions in talk — health beliefs are performed in conversation, not stored in minds
Discursive Psychology — quantitative methods का समर्थन करती है
Harré और Potter — identical theoretical positions रखते हैं

explanation: Harré (1979) — Positioning Theory: positions in conversation rather than fixed roles। Potter & Wetherell (1987) — Discourse Analysis: language constructs social reality, not merely reflects mental states। Challenge to social cognition: (1) Attitudes are not stored but constructed in context, (2) 'Health attitudes' vary with interlocutor, purpose, accountability, (3) Identity is achieved discursively, not possessed. Health Application: KAP surveys miss discursive construction of 'attitudes'. FGD discourse analysis → how health beliefs are negotiated in community talk। Conversation Analysis of medical encounters → turn-taking reveals power dynamics।

question: 'Prevention Paradox' (Rose) और 'High-Risk Strategy vs Population Strategy' में social psychology का tension क्या है?

options.text: Population strategy — हमेशा high-risk strategy से better है
Population strategy: small benefit to many > large benefit to few (mathematically); but psychologically — individuals have little personal benefit perception → low motivation and political resistance
Prevention Paradox — psychological dimension नहीं है
High-Risk strategy — always most cost-effective

explanation: Geoffrey Rose (1985) — Prevention Paradox: most cases of disease come from 'average risk' populations (numerically more), not high-risk. Population strategy (shift entire distribution) → greatest impact. BUT: psychological paradox: lowering salt for ALL → personal benefit tiny ('sick individual' treatment very salient, 'statistical life' invisible). Political: policy unpopular (no personal motivation). High-risk: visible, motivated individuals. Behavioral economics application: default healthy options (salt reduction), taxation (nudge), social norms shifts. India में: national programs must address both but explain population benefit clearly।

question: Judith Butler का 'Performativity' और 'Gender Trouble' सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में gender और health की समझ को कैसे radically transform करता है?

options.text: Butler — gender को biological reality के रूप में confirm करती हैं
Gender = iterative performative acts (not fixed essence) → gender norms construct differential health risks, access, and treatments — destabilizing binaries opens new health possibilities
Performativity Theory — केवल LGBTQ+ individuals में applicable
Butler की theory — empirical health research में inapplicable है

explanation: Judith Butler (1990) — Gender Trouble: Gender not a noun (identity) but a verb (doing). Performativity: repeated citations of gender norms produce the illusion of a stable gender identity. Subversion through parody, drag. Health implications: (1) 'Men don't cry' = health-damaging gender performance, (2) 'Women as primary caregivers' = burnout, (3) Trans health — non-binary bodies destabilize binary medical protocols, (4) Intersex 'normalizing' surgeries — enforcing gender binary, (5) PCPNDT Act — response to son preference = gender performativity normalization। Queer theory → inclusive health systems।

question: 'Social Epidemiology' में 'Psychosocial Pathway' बनाम 'Neo-material Pathway' debate स्वास्थ्य असमानताओं की causation में क्या resolve करती है?

options.text: दोनों pathways identical explanations देती हैं
Psychosocial: relative deprivation → stress hormones → disease; Neo-material: absolute deprivation → lack of resources → disease — both operate, best evidence: interaction model
Neo-material Pathway — has been conclusively proven; psychosocial — disproven
Psychosocial pathway — only mental health में relevant है

explanation: Debate: Wilkinson & Pickett (2009) — psychosocial: income inequality → status anxiety → stress biology → poor health. Critics (Lynch, Kaplan) — neo-material: poverty → lack of food, housing, healthcare → direct disease causation. Marmot — Whitehall studies support psychosocial (controlling for material resources, gradient persists). Resolution: both operate, income inequality works through BOTH material deprivation AND psychosocial pathways. Policy implications: income inequality reduction (material AND psychosocial), not just poverty elimination. India में: relative deprivation in aspirational middle class + absolute deprivation in poor।

question: Moscovici और Mugny के 'Conversion Theory' में minority influence के 'conversion effect' और 'compliance effect' में क्या difference है और यह health advocacy में कैसे relevant है?

options.text: Conversion और Compliance — identical outcomes हैं

Compliance — public behavior change without private attitude change (majority influence); Conversion — private attitude change without public acknowledgment (minority influence) — delayed, indirect health impact
Minority influence — केवल compliance produces करती है
Majority influence — always more powerful than minority influence

explanation: Moscovici & Mugny — Majority influence: normative route → public compliance, no private conversion। Minority influence: informational/consistency route → private attitude change (conversion) even if not publicly admitted. Delayed action and indirect validation. Health advocacy: (1) Early vaccine advocates (minority) → gradual conversion → mainstream, (2) Mental health anti-stigma advocates — initially minority → conversion of health professionals, (3) Family planning pioneers in conservative communities — minorities create cognitive conflict → private reconsideration। WHO advocates often minority voices → conversion takes decades but transforms policy।

question: 'Moral Disengagement' (Bandura) theory का स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली में corruption और unethical behavior को explain करने में क्या योगदान है?

options.text: Moral Disengagement — केवल war crimes में applicable
8 mechanisms (moral justification, euphemistic labeling, dehumanization, displacement of responsibility, etc.) allow health workers to harm without guilt — systemic, not just individual
Moral Disengagement — individual character flaw है, systemic नहीं
Bandura ने moral disengagement को health ethics में apply नहीं किया

explanation: Bandura (1999) — Moral Disengagement: 8 mechanisms: (1) Moral justification ('prescribing unnecessary tests saves lives'), (2) Euphemistic labeling ('enhancement fee' not bribe), (3) Advantageous comparison ('everyone does it'), (4) Displacement of responsibility ('hospital policy'), (5) Diffusion of responsibility ('everyone prescribes this'), (6) Dehumanization ('patients don't understand'), (7) Attribution of blame ('they didn't follow advice'), (8) Disregard for consequences। India में: medical over-prescription, sex-selective abortion facilitation, unauthorized health workers — all use moral disengagement. Institutional ethics cultures counter this।

question: Daniel Kahneman के 'Focusing Illusion' का स्वास्थ्य प्रासंगिकता क्या है और health policy में इसकी implications क्या हैं?

options.text: Focusing Illusion — attention bias का synonym मात्र है
'Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it' — health surveys, quality of life measures, और disability acceptance को systematically distort करती है
Focusing Illusion — health में positive outcomes देती है
Kahneman की Focusing Illusion — प्रयोगात्मक रूप से unsupported है

explanation: Kahneman et al. (2006) — Focusing Illusion: जिस पर ध्यान केंद्रित है, उसे overweight किया जाता है। Health implications: (1) Pre-illness people overestimate disability's impact on well-being (Impact Bias + Focusing Illusion), (2) Disability paradox: people with severe disabilities report better QoL than non-disabled people expect, (3) Health policy: stated preferences for health states exaggerate importance when health is salient, (4) Cancer patients' daily well-being ≠ retrospective global ratings, (5) 'Day Reconstruction Method' vs retrospective surveys। India में: disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) — methodological caution।

question: Dacher Keltner के 'Power Paradox' का स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली में power-holding health officials के behaviour पर क्या निहितार्थ है?

options.text: Power — health officials में empathy बढ़ाती है
Power → empathy deficit, risk-taking, disinhibition, stereotyping, attention narrowing — powerful health officers बनते हैं less effective community servants
Power Paradox — केवल political leaders में
Power holders — naturally better decision-makers बनते हैं

explanation: Keltner (2016) — Power Paradox: Power gained through empathy, collaboration, social intelligence; BUT power corrupts these very qualities. Neural level: power → reduced mirror neuron activity → empathy deficit (Van Kleef studies). Behavioral: powerful → more stereotyping, less perspective-taking, more rule-breaking, attention narrowing. Health system: CMO/District Health Officer → over time → less community-connected, patient experiences invisible. Power Approach Theory (Keltner): power → approach motivation system activation → action without social caution. Counter: distributed power, accountability, community feedback mechanisms।

question: Sherif का 'Realistic Group Conflict Theory' और Gaertner का 'Common Ingroup Identity Model' — दोनों के बीच के theoretical tension का मूल्यांकन करें।

options.text: दोनों theories identical conclusions देती हैं

RGCT: competition for real resources → conflict; CIIM: recategorize as one superordinate group → prejudice reduction — tension: CIIM may erase important subgroup identities and ignore real resource competition
CIIM — RGCT को complete replacement है
Realistic Group Conflict — modern multicultural societies में inapplicable

explanation: Sherif (1954) RGCT: Scarce resources → intergroup competition → hostility. Solution: superordinate goals. Gaertner et al. CIIM: Recategorize warring groups as single superordinate group → reduce bias. Tension: (1) CIIM may demand subgroup identity erasure → identity threat (Dovidio), (2) 'Dual identity' model (both superordinate + subgroup) better, (3) RGCT: if resources actually scarce, recategorization not enough. Health in: caste groups competing for PHC posts → RGCT. Superordinate 'community health' identity → CIIM. Both needed: resource equity (RGCT-informed) + inclusive identity (CIIM-informed)।

question: Clifford Geertz की 'Thick Description' methodology और सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान की experimental tradition के बीच epistemological conflict का स्वास्थ्य अनुसंधान में क्या समाधान है?

options.text: Thick Description — scientific health research में inapplicable है
Mixed Methods Integration: Thick Description reveals cultural context और meaning; experiment tests mechanisms — complementary epistemologies through pragmatic triangulation
Geertz ने experimental psychology को fully support किया
Thick Description और experiment — never compatible

explanation: Geertz (1973) — Thick Description: interpretive ethnography capturing layers of meaning in cultural context — 'what is a wink?' depends on context, intention, shared understanding. Epistemological conflict with positivism: (1) Context-specificity vs generalizability, (2) Interpretation vs measurement, (3) Emic vs etic. Health research resolution: (1) Phase 1: ethnographic thick description → hypotheses, (2) Phase 2: experimental test, (3) Phase 3: return to context for implementation. Community Intervention: understanding 'why people don't seek TB care' requires thick description + epidemiological data + intervention trial। Sequential mixed methods।

question: 'Post-Colonial Psychology' (Fanon, Bulhan) ने mainstream Western Social Psychology को किन आधारों पर challenge किया है?

options.text: Post-Colonial Psychology — Western psychology को fully accepts करती है
Western SP: WEIRD-biased, colonial knowledge structures reproduced, Indigenous psychologies marginalized, psychology itself as colonial tool — decolonization needed
Post-Colonial Psychology — केवल African contexts में relevant है
Fanon — psychological theories नहीं दिए, केवल political writing किया

explanation: Fanon (1952, 1961) — Wretched of the Earth: colonization → psychological damage (internalized racism, Manichaean worldview, colonial personality). Hussein Bulhan — Zones of Nonbeing. Challenges to mainstream SP: (1) WEIRD samples → universal claims, (2) Colonial researchers studying colonized = extraction, (3) Individualism embedded in Western SP vs relational African/Asian psychologies, (4) Western categories (mental illness, personality) impose on different ontologies. India में: indigenous health systems (Ayurveda, tribal healing) pathologized by Western psychiatry. Decolonizing Health Psychology: community-based, indigenous-methods, power-reflexive।

question: Edward Deci और Richard Ryan के 'Organismic Integration Theory' (OIT) में internalization की प्रक्रिया health behavior adherence में क्यों central है?

options.text: OIT — SDT का irrelevant subdivision है
Internalization continuum (Introjection → Identification → Integration) determines regulation quality — integrated regulation = most autonomous, most sustainable health behavior
OIT — external motivation को best मानती है
Health behavior — केवल external regulation से effective होती है

explanation: OIT (Deci & Ryan) — sub-theory of SDT explaining how external regulation becomes progressively internalized: (1) External (reward/punishment) → (2) Introjected (internal pressure, guilt, pride) → (3) Identified (personally meaningful) → (4) Integrated (consistent with self). Quality of motivation matters more than quantity. Health in: (1) Diabetes management forced by doctor (external) → drops when unsupervised, (2) 'Healthy eating = part of who I am' (integrated) → sustained, (3) Nurse supporting patient autonomy → facilitates internalization, (4) Community health programs — build identification then integration। Autonomy-supportive environments accelerate internalization।

question: 'Cognitive Polyphasia' (Moscovici) की अवधारणा और भारतीय समुदायों में Western medicine और traditional health beliefs के सह-अस्तित्व को explain करने में इसका उपयोग क्या है?

options.text: Cognitive Polyphasia — cognitive inconsistency है, irrational है
Cognitive Polyphasia: different, contradictory modes of thinking co-exist in same person for different purposes — rational, not pathological — explains medical pluralism naturally
Cognitive Polyphasia — केवल pre-modern societies में
Modern education eliminates Cognitive Polyphasia

explanation: Moscovici (1961, 1976) — Cognitive Polyphasia: multiple, sometimes contradictory logics coexist within individuals — different modes for different social contexts. Not confusion, but adaptive flexibility. India health in: same woman → Ayurvedic remedies for chronic conditions (traditional logic) + antibiotics for acute infection (biomedical logic) + religious rituals for 'nazar' (religious logic). All three coexist rationally in different contexts. Implications: (1) Don't force choice between systems, (2) Understand when/why each mode activated, (3) Integrate biomedical and traditional — not compete।

question: Roy Baumeister का 'Meaning-Making Theory' existential health psychology में कैसे applies होता है?

options.text: Meaning-Making — केवल psychotherapy में, public health में नहीं
4 needs for meaning (Purpose, Values, Efficacy, Self-Worth) — chronic illness, disability, bereavement में meaning disruption → psychological distress; restoration → resilience and health
Baumeister — Frankl के logotherapy का identical extension
Meaning-Making — passive process है, active नहीं

explanation: Baumeister (1991) — Meaning and motivation: 4 needs: (1) Purpose (goals/fulfillment), (2) Values (moral worth), (3) Efficacy (sense of control), (4) Self-Worth (belonging, justification). Illness threatens all 4. Park (2010) — Meaning-Making Model: global meaning (worldview) + situational meaning (appraisal) → discrepancy → meaning-making coping → revised global meaning. Health: cancer diagnosis → purpose loss + worldview shattered → meaning-making process → post-traumatic growth. Palliative care: dignity therapy, narrative life review. ASHA worker burnout → meaning erosion → intervention needed।

question: Philip Zimbardo के Stanford Prison Experiment की पुनर्व्याख्या और 'situationism vs dispositionalism' debate में आधुनिक social neuroscience क्या योगदान देती है?

options.text: Stanford Prison Experiment — perfect science है, पुनर्व्याख्या अनावश्यक
SPE — methodological flaws (experimenter demand, selection bias); modern view: person-situation interaction, not pure situationism; neural substrates of role-conformity emerging
SPE — dispositionalist view को confirm करता है
Situationism — modern neuroscience ने completely disproved किया

explanation: SPE (Zimbardo, 1971) — guards became brutal in 6 days. Original claim: situation overwhelms disposition. Critiques: (1) Demand characteristics — guards coached, (2) Selection bias — power-seeking participants, (3) Experimenter role confusion, (4) Parry reanalysis (2018). Reicher & Haslam (2006) BBC Prison Study: guards not automatically brutal — identity-based, (5) Modern view: person × situation interaction (Fleeson's whole-trait theory). Social Neuroscience: role adoption activates identity-consistent neural networks. Health: 'healthy/sick role' neural consolidation. Institutionalization of both patients and staff।

question: Roy Baumeister का 'Ego Depletion' और Carol Dweck का 'Growth Mindset' — दोनों health behavior change में कैसे complementary हैं?

options.text: Ego Depletion और Growth Mindset — contradictory, incompatible theories
Ego Depletion: willpower is limited resource; Growth Mindset: belief that willpower grows with use — beliefs about willpower moderate depletion effects — intervention targets both
Ego Depletion — fully replicated, no controversy
Growth Mindset — केवल academic performance में, health में नहीं

explanation: Baumeister Ego Depletion: sequential self-control tasks → depleted → worse performance. Dweck Growth Mindset: 'willpower grows with use.' Job & Dweck (2010): people who believe willpower is non-limited → no depletion! Replication: Ego depletion inconsistently replicated. Together: (1) health behavior interventions should build willpower beliefs (mindset) not just 'try harder,' (2) Structural environments reduce depletion demand (healthy defaults), (3) Replenishment: glucose, positive emotion (but glucose effect also contested). India में: chronic poverty environments → perpetual depletion → structural solutions critical over willpower-building।

question: Hannah Arendt की 'Banality of Evil' अवधारणा और Milgram के obedience को मिलाकर institutional health care में systemic harm को कैसे समझाया जाता है?

options.text: Arendt की theory — health care में completely irrelevant है
Ordinary health workers following routine procedures can cause systemic harm without malicious intent — 'thoughtlessness' and bureaucratic role-following = health's 'banality of evil'
Arendt — individual evil को describe करती हैं, systemic नहीं
Banality of Evil — health system में unobservable है

explanation: Hannah Arendt (1963) — Eichmann in Jerusalem: 'banality of evil' — not monster, but bureaucratic functionary following orders without moral thinking. Thoughtlessness as danger. Health Applications: (1) Nurses documenting vitals routinely while patient deteriorates — 'not my job to question,' (2) Tuskegee — researchers following protocol without moral reflection, (3) Forced sterilizations in India — officials following government targets, (4) Psychiatric institutionalization harm. Milgram extends empirically. Prevention: cultivate moral awareness, reflective practice, professional courage, ethics training, safe whistleblowing।

question: Tajfel का 'Minimal Group Paradigm' (MGP) in-group favoritism के बारे में क्या radical finding reveal करता है और इसकी theoretical implications क्या हैं?

options.text: MGP दिखाता है कि in-group favoritism — केवल long-standing cultural groups में
Even trivially created groups (random assignment, dot-estimating) show in-group favoritism — discrimination is automatic, minimal basis needed — self-categorization sufficient
MGP — prejudice की absence demonstrate करता है
In-group favoritism — केवल competitive contexts में होती है

explanation: Tajfel et al. (1971) — MGP: Participants arbitrarily assigned to groups (dot-overestimators vs underestimators). Even with minimal criteria: allocate more points to in-group, even sacrificing absolute gains for relative advantage. Finding: discrimination requires NO real differences, history, or conflict — mere categorization sufficient. SIT explanation: positive distinctiveness seeking → self-esteem via in-group superiority. Implications: (1) Healthcare discrimination may occur with minimal group cues (uniform, dialect), (2) Very difficult to eliminate — structural interventions needed, (3) Superordinate identity strategies (CIIM) must overcome this basic mechanism।

question: 'Cultural Neuroscience' (Chiao & Bebko) के निष्कर्ष social psychology के cross-cultural generalizations को कैसे challenge करते हैं?

options.text: Cultural Neuroscience — culture-universal brain mechanisms confirm करती है

Neural processes underlying social cognition (self, pain perception, fairness) are culturally shaped — same stimuli, different neural activation — challenges universal claims of Western social psychology
Cultural Neuroscience — brain structure को culture से independent मानती है
Cultural Neuroscience — theoretical, no empirical evidence

explanation: Chiao & Bebko (2011) — Cultural Neuroscience: culture × biology interaction. Evidence: (1) Self-referential processing — East Asians: medial PFC activates for close others AND self; Westerners: only self. (2) Pain empathy — in-group vs out-group neural differences. (3) Fairness norms — Ultimatum Game: different neural responses across cultures. (4) Collectivism gene-culture coevolution (serotonin transporter polymorphism). Implications: (1) Social psychology theories (even social cognition) culturally situated, (2) Health interventions must match cultural neurocognitive patterns, (3) WEIRD neuroscience ≠ universal।

question: 'Liberation Psychology' (Martín-Baró) और 'Community Psychology' (Sarason) — दोनों mainstream social psychology के वैकल्पिक approaches कैसे हैं?

options.text: दोनों mainstream social psychology के identical हैं

Liberation Psych: psychology must serve oppressed, not oppressors — deconstruct ideological falsehoods, recover historical memory, prefer poor; Community Psych: ecological view, prevention, community change over individual treatment
Liberation Psychology — political ideology है, science नहीं
Community Psychology — केवल mental health में, physical health में नहीं

explanation: Ignacio Martín-Baró (1994) — Liberation Psychology from El Salvador: (1) Deconstruct oppressive social reality, (2) Recover historical memory of oppressed, (3) Preferential option for poor, (4) Deideologize — expose false consciousness. Seymour Sarason — Community Psychology (1974): sense of community, ecological analysis, prevention over treatment. Together: health psychology must (1) Work WITH marginalized communities, (2) Address structural conditions, (3) Build community competence, (4) Prevention focus. India में: Eklavya Foundation, SEWA health programs, Chhattisgarh community health movement — liberation approach।

question: Naomi Zack का 'Philosophy of Race' और 'Race as Social Construction' का biological health research में क्या implications है?

options.text: Race — purely biological category है

Race is socially constructed but has real health effects through racism (stress, discrimination, differential treatment) — biological race in medicine is scientifically invalid but racism is real health determinant
Race-based medicine — fully scientific है
Race = ethnicity — दोनों identical concepts

explanation: Naomi Zack — Race has no biological validity (genetic variation within 'races' > between). BUT race as social category has profound health effects through: (1) Racism-related stress → allostatic load (Geronimus — 'weathering'), (2) Discrimination in healthcare → differential treatment, pain mismanagement, (3) Residential segregation → environmental exposures, (4) Epigenetic effects of chronic discrimination. Dangers of race-based medicine: (1) eGFR race correction in kidney disease — perpetuates inequality (now being removed), (2) BiDil — first 'race-based drug' — controversial. India में: caste ≈ race in health effects। 'Racism not race causes health disparities.'।

question: Antonio Damasio का 'Somatic Marker Hypothesis' rational health decision-making के बारे में क्या reveal करता है?

options.text: Damasio — pure reason health decisions में sufficient है
Somatic markers (embodied emotional signals from past experience) guide decision-making — without them, rational health decisions become impossible, not better (Descartes' Error)
Somatic Marker Hypothesis — behavior therapy का extension है
Emotions always impair health decision-making

explanation: Damasio (1994) — Descartes' Error: Ventromedial PFC patients (emotion-processing damage) → preserve intellect but catastrophic real-life decisions (gambling, relationships). Somatic markers: body-based emotional signals from associated past experiences guide future choices, narrowing option space before rational deliberation. Health implications: (1) Fear response to needle → avoidance (somatic marker from past pain), (2) Affective computing in health AI must account for emotional decision guidance, (3) Health communication must engage emotional system, not just cognitive, (4) Patients with chronic disease develop somatic markers for treatment experiences → adherence affected।

question: Zygmunt Bauman का 'Liquid Modernity' और 'Liquid Surveillance' आधुनिक digital health में क्या challenges उत्पन्न करते हैं?

options.text: Bauman — positive view of digital health surveillance रखते थे

Liquid modernity: unstable identities, dissolved communities, fragmented social bonds → health misinformation spreads faster; liquid surveillance: health data flows without consent, new forms of health control
Liquid Modernity — pre-digital concept है, आज irrelevant
Bauman का work — health में applicability नहीं रखता

explanation: Bauman (2000) — Liquid Modernity: solid institutions dissolve → flexibility, insecurity, individualism. Health implications: (1) Community health solidarity weakens in liquid modernity → individualized health consumerism, (2) Solid professional health authority → liquid (social media 'experts' equally credible), (3) Stable identities → fluid health identities (wellness influencer vs patient). Liquid Surveillance (Bauman & Lyon, 2013): surveillance flows, seeps into daily life — wearables, health apps → gentle coercion into 'responsible health citizenship.' India में: Aarogya Setu → digital health liquid surveillance। Privacy, consent, health data justice।

question: Michael White का 'Narrative Therapy' और Deconstructionist approach सामाजिक मनोविज्ञान में dominant health narratives को कैसे challenge करते हैं?

options.text: Narrative Therapy — biological model का complement मात्र है
Externalizing the problem, deconstructing dominant pathologizing narratives, and restoring preferred identity stories — power dynamics in health narratives are explicitly interrogated
Narrative Therapy — केवल mental illness में
White और Epston — cognitive therapy की branch हैं

explanation: Michael White & David Epston (1990) — Narrative Therapy: (1) Externalizing: problem is not the person — 'the diabetes' not 'you're diabetic,' (2) Deconstruction: whose story is this? (medical discourse vs patient's experience), (3) Unique outcomes: exceptions to problem-saturated story → build alternative story, (4) Definitional ceremony: witnessing by community. Deconstructionist: challenges dominant biomedical narrative that positions patient as passive, deficient, non-compliant. Health applications: (1) Chronic illness — preferred identity restoration, (2) Addiction — externalizing 'the addiction,' (3) Disability — challenging tragedy narrative, (4) Community health — collective preferred identity।

question: 'Cultural Consonance' (Dressler) बनाम 'Cultural Incongruity' (Oyserman) — दोनों concepts मिलकर health behavior को कैसे predict करते हैं?

options.text: Cultural Consonance और Cultural Incongruity — opposing theories हैं

Consonance: living up to cultural models reduces stress → better health; Incongruity (identity-behavior mismatch): when context activates identity inconsistent with behavior → motivation to change — both predict health behavior
Dressler और Oyserman — identical constructs describe करते हैं
Cultural factors — health behavior prediction में unimportant हैं

explanation: Dressler — Cultural Consonance: shared cultural models (ideal body, food practices) → lived consonance = stress buffer → better health. Oyserman — Cultural Incongruity/Culture as Situated Cognition: identity salience in context → if cued identity inconsistent with health behavior → dissonance → motivation to change ('student identity' + 'healthy student' schema cued → more studying, healthier eating). Together: (1) Consonance with cultural health ideals = protective, (2) Incongruity intervention: 'as a mother, what would you do for your child's health?' — cue maternal identity. India में: 'good farmer' identity + healthy farm practices।

question: Ann Oakley का 'Sociology of Housework' और feminist critique — reproductive health में 'medicalization of birth' को कैसे explain करती है?

options.text: Medicalization of birth — purely positive public health achievement है
Medicalization: normal female bodily processes (pregnancy, birth) redefined as medical events → male medical control, surveillance, disempowerment of women — feminist critique essential
Oakley — medical intervention in birth को fully supports करती हैं
Feminist critique — birth medicalization में inapplicable है

explanation: Ann Oakley (1980) — 'Women Confined': hospital birth → medicalization → loss of women's control. Conrad (2007) — Medicalization: non-medical conditions redefined as medical. Birth medicalization: (1) Normal birth → pathologized risk, (2) Male obstetrician replaces female midwife, (3) Technology (fetal monitoring, epidurals) → passive patient, (4) Caesarean rate explosion (India: 47% private sector). Feminist critique: (1) Women's birth autonomy violated, (2) TBA/midwife marginalization → traditional knowledge erased, (3) Respectful maternity care. India: LaQshya program — respectful, woman-centered. Counter: some medicalization saves lives — critical feminism, not rejection।

question: René Girard का 'Scapegoat Theory' और 'Mimetic Desire' — महामारियों में community violence और stigma को explain करने में कैसे apply होते हैं?

options.text: Girard — केवल anthropological, health में inapplicable
Mimetic desire creates social tension → surrogate victim (scapegoat) needed → epidemic periods: stigmatized groups become sacrificial — historical pattern repeats
Mimetic Desire — economic competition से completely different है
Scapegoat Theory — Allport के prejudice theory का identical है

explanation: René Girard (1972) — Mimetic Desire: we desire what others desire → rivalry → social crisis। Resolution: surrogate victim (scapegoat) — unite against common 'culprit.' Health epidemics: (1) Black Death → Jewish scapegoating, (2) AIDS → gay men, Africans, (3) COVID India → minorities, migrants, NE Indians, healthcare workers. Pattern: social anxiety + visible 'other' + mimetic community solidarity → violence/exclusion. Girard: scapegoating is universal, disguised as legitimate response. Health Communication: identify scapegoating early, provide factual attribution, build inclusive community identity. Media responsibility critical।

question: Erving Goffman के 'Total Institutions' की अवधारणा का आधुनिक psychiatric hospitals और long-term care facilities में क्या relevance है?

options.text: Total Institutions — historical concept, modern healthcare में irrelevant
Mortification of self (stripping identity), standardization, surveillance — modern mental health institutions और care homes partially retain these features → dehumanization → poor outcomes
Goffman — psychiatric institutions को supportive बताते थे
Total Institution features — patient outcomes पर no impact

explanation: Goffman (1961) — 'Asylums': Total institutions encompass all aspects of life under single authority. 4 processes: (1) Mortification of self — stripping names, clothes, personal history, (2) Standardization — uniform routines regardless of individuality, (3) Surveillance — constant visibility, (4) Privilege systems — rewards for compliance. Modern relevance: (1) Psychiatric wards — still partially total, (2) COVID isolation centers in India — totalizing, (3) Long-term care homes — infantilization, (4) Prisons as health environments. Counter: Recovery Model, Deinstitutionalization, Person-Centered Care, Therapeutic Community approaches।

question: 'Positive Health' (Seligman) और 'Salutogenesis' (Antonovsky) के बीच theoretical convergences और divergences क्या हैं?

options.text: Positive Health और Salutogenesis — completely identical frameworks हैं

Both: beyond pathology, focus on assets and well-being; Divergence: Antonovsky — sense of coherence (comprehensibility, manageability, meaningfulness); Seligman — PERMA + physical assets — different operationalizations
Salutogenesis — pathogenic model का extension है
Positive Health — population level, Salutogenesis — individual only

explanation: Aaron Antonovsky (1979) — Salutogenesis: What keeps people healthy despite stressors? Sense of Coherence (SOC): comprehensibility (makes sense), manageability (resources available), meaningfulness (worth the effort). Generalized Resistance Resources. Seligman (2008) — Positive Health: well-being (PERMA: Positive emotion, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, Accomplishment) + physical and biological assets. Convergences: both asset-based, both see health as positive state. Divergences: SOC = cognitive-motivational orientation; PERMA = multidimensional well-being. India में: SOC for community resilience programs; PERMA for HEO wellness programs।

question: Foucault के 'Biopower' और 'Biopolitics' की अवधारणाओं का India के population health programs में क्या critical analysis होता है?

options.text: Biopower — purely positive state tool for health improvement है

State deployment of power over life (discipline of individual bodies + regulation of populations) — family planning programs, immunization campaigns, COVID lockdowns = biopolitical governance with compliance/resistance tensions
Biopower — केवल authoritarian states में होता है
Foucault — public health को fully supports करते थे

explanation: Foucault (1975, 1978) — Biopower: power over life. Two poles: (1) Anatomo-politics (discipline of individual body — clinical gaze, sexuality regulation), (2) Biopolitics (regulation of population — birth rates, mortality, migration). India in: (1) Emergency sterilization (1975-77) — extreme anatomo-politics, (2) Immunization campaigns — both beneficial AND disciplinary, (3) BMI surveillance in schools, (4) COVID lockdowns — intense biopolitical intervention, (5) ABHA health ID — permanent biopolitical data extraction. Critical health: biopolitical programs must ensure consent, equity, resistance rights. Not rejection but critical consciousness।

question: Michael Marmot का 'Status Syndrome' hypothesis और Wilkinson का 'Spirit Level' — दोनों को empirically और theoretically कैसे evaluate किया जाता है?

options.text: दोनों theories — empirically uncontested हैं
